name: Zagreb
tagline: Croatia's underrated capital, a Central European city of tiled church roofs, quirky museums and a café culture the coast rarely gets credit for.
highlight: Sitting for a slow coffee on Tkalčićeva Street, the whole city seemingly in no hurry to be anywhere else.
shortDescription: Croatia's underrated Central European capital, home to St Mark's colourfully tiled church roof, the Museum of Broken Relationships and a genuine café culture.
metaDescription: A Zagreb travel guide: St Mark's Church, Ban Jelačić Square, Dolac Market, the Upper Town, food and how to plan a visit to Croatia's capital.
knownFor: St Mark's Church, Ban Jelačić Square, the Upper Town

image.file: File:Church of St. Mark and Coat of arms of Zagreb on southern roof (13024345783).jpg
image.alt: St Mark's Church in Zagreb's Upper Town

intro: Zagreb is Croatia's most underrated city, a Central European capital most visitors skip entirely on their way to the coast, to their own real loss.

Its Upper Town preserves a compact medieval core, crowned by St Mark's Church and its instantly recognisable tiled roof, while the Lower Town's grid of Austro-Hungarian boulevards holds museums, parks and squares.

What Zagreb does best is a slower pace than the coast — long coffees on Tkalčićeva Street, a proper daily market at Dolac, and a lively, youthful energy that runs year-round rather than just in summer.

whyVisit.intro: Zagreb's case rests on being a real, lived-in Central European capital rather than a coastal resort.

points.title: St Mark's Church is one of the country's iconic images
points.text: Its colourful tiled roof displaying the coats of arms of Zagreb and Croatia.

points.title: The café culture is a real daily ritual
points.text: Tkalčićeva Street and beyond built around lingering, unhurried coffee.

points.title: It's full of quirky, memorable museums
points.text: The Museum of Broken Relationships and others go well beyond standard city-break fare.

points.title: It works well year-round
points.text: Unlike the seasonal coast, Zagreb stays lively through every month of the year.

points.title: It's an easy gateway to Plitvice Lakes
points.text: Croatia's most famous national park sits about two hours away by road.

attractionsIntro: Zagreb's essential sights are split between the historic Upper Town and the grid-planned Lower Town below it.

attractions.name: St Mark's Church

image.file: File:Church of St. Mark and Coat of arms of Zagreb on southern roof (13024345783).jpg
image.alt: St Mark's Church and its colourfully tiled roof in Zagreb

attractions.text: The city's most photographed landmark, its tiled roof displaying the coats of arms of Zagreb and the Triune Kingdom.
attractions.tip: The small square out front gets crowded — visit early for photos without a crowd in frame.

attractions.name: Zagreb Cathedral
attractions.text: The country's tallest building, its twin neo-Gothic spires visible across much of the city.
attractions.tip: A short walk from Dolac Market — an easy pairing for a morning wander.

attractions.name: Ban Jelačić Square

image.alt: Ban Jelačić Square, the heart of Zagreb

attractions.text: The city's central meeting point, a grand square named for the 19th-century ban whose statue dominates it.
attractions.tip: A natural starting point for exploring both the Upper and Lower Towns.

attractions.name: Dolac Market
attractions.text: A real, working farmers' market, its red umbrellas covering stalls of fresh produce, cheese and flowers.
attractions.tip: Go in the morning, when the market is at its freshest and liveliest.

attractions.name: Lotrščak Tower

image.alt: Lotrščak Tower in Zagreb's Upper Town

attractions.text: A medieval defensive tower, famous today for a cannon still fired from its top every day at noon.
attractions.tip: Climb up for one of the best views over the Lower Town's rooftops.

attractions.name: The Stone Gate

image.alt: The Stone Gate, a shrine in Zagreb's old city walls

attractions.text: The only surviving gate from the medieval city walls, now home to a revered shrine to the Virgin Mary.
attractions.tip: A quiet, atmospheric stop, often with candles lit by visitors passing through.

attractions.name: The Museum of Broken Relationships

image.alt: The Museum of Broken Relationships in Zagreb

attractions.text: One of the city's most memorable, unusual museums, objects and stories donated from real failed relationships worldwide.
attractions.tip: Allow more time than you'd expect — the stories are absorbing.

thingsToDoIntro: Zagreb rewards a slower pace, built around markets, museums and a proper café culture.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the Lotrščak Tower's noon cannon

image.alt: The top of Lotrščak Tower in Zagreb

thingsToDo.text: A fun daily ritual, a cannon fired from the tower every day at exactly noon, a tradition dating back generations.
thingsToDo.tip: Time your Upper Town visit to be nearby at midday for the moment itself.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Tkalčićeva Street
thingsToDo.text: An essential Zagreb experience, a pedestrian street lined with cafés built for exactly this kind of slow wandering.
thingsToDo.tip: At its liveliest in the early evening, when locals fill every outdoor table.

thingsToDo.title: Browse Dolac Market

image.alt: Browsing the stalls at Dolac Market in Zagreb

thingsToDo.text: An authentic slice of daily Zagreb life, browsing stalls of fresh produce, cheese and flowers.
thingsToDo.tip: A great spot to pick up picnic supplies or local cheese to take home.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the Museum of Broken Relationships

image.file: File:Zagreb 's Museum of Broken Relationships second room.jpg
image.alt: Exhibits at the Museum of Broken Relationships in Zagreb

thingsToDo.text: An unusual, moving hour, reading real stories behind donated objects from relationships around the world.
thingsToDo.tip: Worth going in without reading too much beforehand — let the exhibits surprise you.

thingsToDo.title: Touch the Stone Gate's shrine

image.alt: The shrine within Zagreb's Stone Gate

thingsToDo.text: A quiet, reflective stop, joining locals who still stop to pray as they pass through.
thingsToDo.tip: Keep your voice down — this remains an active, respected place of devotion.

thingsToDo.title: Sit for coffee on Ban Jelačić Square

image.file: File:Tram Ban Josip Jelacic Square in Zagreb, Croatia.jpg

thingsToDo.text: An essential Zagreb pastime, watching the city's trams and crowds go by from a square-side café.
thingsToDo.tip: A good spot to get your bearings before heading up to the Upper Town.

foodIntro: Zagreb's food leans more Central European than the coast, with its own distinct specialities.

foods.name: Zagrebački odrezak (Zagreb-style schnitzel)

image.alt: Zagrebački odrezak, a breaded veal schnitzel stuffed with ham and cheese

foods.text: The city's namesake dish, a breaded veal cutlet stuffed with ham and cheese.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants throughout the Lower Town.

foods.name: Štrukli
foods.text: A beloved regional specialty, thin dough layered with cottage cheese, baked or boiled.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants throughout the city, especially in the Upper Town.

foods.name: Ćevapi

image.alt: Ćevapi, grilled minced meat skewers popular across Croatia

foods.text: A reliable, inexpensive classic, grilled minced meat served with flatbread and onion.
foods.whereToTry: Casual restaurants throughout the city centre.

foods.name: Kremšnita (custard cream cake)
foods.text: A nearby regional favourite from Samobor, layers of custard and cream between crisp pastry.

foods.name: Croatian wine
foods.text: Worth exploring in Zagreb's wine bars, with continental Croatia's whites alongside coastal reds.
foods.whereToTry: Wine bars throughout the Lower Town.

foods.name: Fritule (small fried doughnuts)
foods.text: A nice sweet treat, found at bakeries and cafés throughout the city.

accommodation.intro: Zagreb offers noticeably better value than the coast, with everything of interest within easy reach of the centre.

areas.name: Lower Town, near Ban Jelačić Square
areas.bestFor: Being central and within walking distance of most sights
areas.text: The most convenient base, close to the Upper Town, Dolac and the main museums.

areas.name: Upper Town (Gornji Grad)
areas.bestFor: A quieter, more atmospheric historic stay
areas.text: Fewer accommodation options, but right among the city's oldest streets.

gettingThere.intro: Zagreb is well connected by air and rail to the rest of Europe, and by road to the Dalmatian coast.

options.text: Available from many European cities year-round.
options.detail: Zagreb Airport sits about 30 minutes from the city centre.

options.text: A comfortable option from Vienna, Budapest or Ljubljana.
options.detail: Journey times range from about two to six hours depending on the route.

options.mode: Bus or car to the Dalmatian coast
options.detail: About five to six hours to Split, or a shorter hop to Plitvice Lakes.

gettingAround.intro: Zagreb's compact centre is easily walkable, with trams and a funicular covering the rest.

options.text: The best way to see the Upper and Lower Towns together.
options.detail: Most major sights sit within a comfortable 20-minute walk of Ban Jelačić Square.

options.text: Useful for reaching neighbourhoods further from the centre.
options.detail: A frequent, easy-to-use network across the wider city.

options.text: One of the shortest funiculars in the world, connecting the Lower and Upper Towns.
options.detail: A fun, quick alternative to the short uphill walk.

bestTime.headline: May, June and September for pleasant weather and a lively city
bestTime.summary: Zagreb is a year-round destination, unlike the seasonal Dalmatian coast.

seasons.text: Mild, comfortable weather with the city at its most pleasant for walking.
Warm, though quieter than usual with many locals away at the coast.
Comfortable weather with the city's cultural calendar back in full swing.
Festive, with one of Europe's best-regarded Christmas markets running through December.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Zagreb works well as a year-round city break.

itinerary.title: Two days in Zagreb
itinerary.intro: Built around the Upper Town's historic sights and the Lower Town's markets and museums.

days.title: The Upper Town
days.summary: St Mark's, the Stone Gate and Lotrščak Tower.
days.morning: St Mark's Church and the surrounding Upper Town streets.
days.afternoon: The Stone Gate and Lotrščak Tower, timed for the noon cannon.
days.evening: Dinner and drinks along Tkalčićeva Street.

days.title: The Lower Town
days.summary: Dolac Market and the city's museums.
days.afternoon: The Museum of Broken Relationships or another city museum.
days.evening: A final dinner near Ban Jelačić Square.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Zagreb visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Time your Upper Town visit for noon to catch the Lotrščak Tower's cannon.
Visit Dolac Market in the morning, when it's at its freshest and liveliest.
Ride the short funicular between the Lower and Upper Towns, just for the novelty.
Book popular restaurants ahead on weekend evenings.
Use Zagreb as an easy base for a Plitvice Lakes day trip.
Expect noticeably better prices than the Dalmatian coast for food and accommodation.

faq.a: Yes — it's an underrated Central European capital with real café culture, quirky museums and a lively year-round atmosphere.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Zagreb?
faq.a: Two to three days covers the Upper and Lower Towns comfortably, with time for a museum or two.

faq.q: Is Zagreb cheaper than the Croatian coast?
faq.a: Yes — accommodation, food and drink all tend to run noticeably cheaper than Dubrovnik or Hvar.

faq.q: Can you day-trip to Plitvice Lakes from Zagreb?
faq.a: Yes — it's about two hours by road, a popular day trip or first stop heading toward the coast.
Yes — the Upper and Lower Towns both sit within easy walking distance of the central square.
Throughout December, widely regarded as one of Europe's best, spread across the Upper and Lower Towns.
